article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 90% indica / 10% sativa
Genetics: Sweet Tooth #3 (ST #3)
Breeder: BC Bud Depot
THC Content: 20–24%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , limonene , and pinene
Primary Flavors: Sweet candy, honey, pear, berry
Flowering Time (Indoor): Approximately 6–7 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Early September
Indoor Yield: High-yielding
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Easy to intermediate

Long before candy-flavored marijuana became an enormous commercial category, Sweet Tooth genetics were already demonstrating how distinctive sweetness could become a strain’s defining feature. BC Sweet Tooth carries that older idea forward in a compact, extremely fast indica format. Its appeal is not built around novelty: the plant was selected as a production cultivar capable of finishing quickly while generating dense, resinous flowers with an unmistakably sugary character.

The aroma can move from honey and ripe pear toward berries, citrus peel, herbs, and earthy spice, while the effects often begin brighter than the 90% indica classification suggests before developing a slower, heavier physical finish. BC Bud Depot continues to emphasize three traits above all others—speed, substantial production, and dense candy-tasting buds—making this weed as much a cultivation-oriented strain as a flavor-driven one.
Genetics and Lineage

The most accurate way to describe the pedigree is an advancement of Sweet Tooth #3. That wording comes directly from BC Bud Depot’s breeder listing and is preferable to simplifying the cultivar into a speculative modern cross. Historical lineage records trace Sweet Tooth #3 through the Sweet Tooth breeding family, which incorporates Sweet Pink Grapefruit and Blueberry -related genetics through repeated breeding and backcrossing. This family tree helps explain why fruit, sugar, berry, and grapefruit-like qualities continue to appear so prominently in descendants of the line.

Sweet Tooth #3 was already a highly developed expression before BC Bud Depot advanced it further. Its ancestry combines the unmistakable aromatic influence of Sweet Pink Grapefruit with genetics descending from Blueberry, whose deeper family tree incorporates Afghani , Thai , and Purple Thai material. Consequently, BC Sweet Tooth should not be viewed simply as a 90% indica selected for sedation. Beneath the short flowering cycle and compact growth lies a diverse old-school genetic background capable of producing floral, fruit, berry, spice, and tropical nuances.

Selection appears to have focused heavily on production efficiency. BC Bud Depot describes the cultivar as one of its preferred production plants, highlighting rapid maturation and heavy crops of dense flower. That emphasis distinguishes it from many collectible marijuana varieties whose unusual terpene expression comes at the cost of long flowering periods or difficult growth. Here, sweetness, speed, and commercial practicality were preserved together.
Effects and Experience

The first phase can be surprisingly lively for cannabis carrying such a strong indica classification. Consumer reports commonly associate BC Sweet Tooth with uplifted and creative sensations before sleepiness becomes more noticeable later in the experience. With a moderate serving, that progression can translate into an easygoing mental lift accompanied by reduced urgency rather than immediate couch-lock. Music, casual conversation, films, and quiet creative activities tend to fit the character better than demanding work requiring sustained precision.

Physical relaxation gradually takes control as the session continues. Shoulders may feel looser, movement becomes less appealing, appetite can increase, and the brighter opening often evolves into a considerably softer, heavier state. BC Bud Depot itself highlights relaxation and appetite stimulation when describing the cultivar. Larger amounts are considerably more likely to push the experience toward drowsiness, making the weed better suited to late afternoon or evening for consumers who respond strongly to indica-dominant marijuana.

Potency deserves respect even though BC Bud Depot does not publish a current laboratory THC figure. Secondary strain data commonly place examples around 24% THC, but cannabinoid concentrations vary by phenotype, cultivation environment, harvest timing, storage, and testing laboratory. THC can alter mood, perception, memory, coordination, and judgment, and high doses may produce anxiety or panic in susceptible individuals. Starting conservatively is especially sensible when the potency of a particular batch is unknown.
Medical Benefits

BC Bud Depot historically promotes BC Sweet Tooth as medicinal cannabis suited to appetite stimulation, pain, and relaxation. Those traditional strain uses are worth documenting, but they do not establish that this particular cultivar has been clinically proven to treat pain, appetite disorders, insomnia, anxiety, or any other medical condition. Strain names do not provide standardized pharmaceutical compositions, and two batches sold under the same name can differ substantially in cannabinoids and terpenes.

Broader cannabinoid research does provide context for several of the symptoms associated with this strain. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health notes that FDA-approved cannabinoid medications containing dronabinol or nabilone are used for chemotherapy-related nausea and vomiting, while dronabinol is also prescribed for appetite and weight-loss problems associated with HIV/AIDS. Evidence also suggests cannabinoids may provide some benefit for certain types of chronic pain, though effectiveness and side effects vary. These findings concern specific cannabinoids and studied preparations rather than BC Sweet Tooth flower itself.

For medical marijuana consumers, the plant’s relaxing nature and tendency to stimulate appetite may therefore be relevant, but higher-THC flower can also cause dizziness, impaired concentration, anxiety, or excessive sedation. Anyone considering cannabis for persistent pain, appetite loss, sleep difficulty, or another diagnosed health problem should discuss its use with an appropriate healthcare professional, particularly when prescription medications or other treatments are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweetness arrives before almost everything else. BC Bud Depot describes the finished buds specifically as having a sweet candy taste, which remains the central sensory feature of the cultivar. Yet properly grown flower usually offers more depth than simple sugar. Consumer and strain-profile data associate it with honey, pear, berry, tree fruit, mild citrus, and earthy accents, producing a softer fruit profile than the aggressive gas and dessert aromas found in many newer cannabis varieties.

Caryophyllene, limonene, and pinene are commonly listed among its prominent terpenes, although BC Bud Depot does not publish an official strain-wide laboratory terpene panel. Caryophyllene can provide a peppery or woody counterpoint to the sugary core, while limonene contributes citrus brightness and pinene introduces fresher herbal or pine-like edges. Expression will change from phenotype to phenotype, which means one harvest may emphasize fruit and honey while another leans more heavily toward spice and greenery.

When smoked or vaporized, the flavor often opens with concentrated sweetness before revealing ripe pear, berry, and faint grapefruit-like acidity. A mild earthy or spicy quality becomes clearer toward the finish, preventing the profile from becoming one-dimensional. Unlike modern candy weed that may resemble syrup, frosting, or artificial fruit, BC Sweet Tooth has an older botanical character in which sweetness remains connected to fruit, herbs, and resin.
Growing Information

Speed is arguably the plant’s most important cultivation trait. BC Bud Depot places indoor flowering at approximately six to seven weeks, while older breeder records list around six weeks and an outdoor harvest from late August into early September. The current breeder page specifies early September for outdoor gardens. Such a short cycle makes the cultivar attractive to growers seeking multiple indoor harvests or outdoor marijuana capable of finishing before prolonged autumn weather becomes a concern.

Its strong indica influence generally favors a controlled, manageable structure rather than extreme flowering stretch. Dense flower formation and rapid bud development make adequate airflow valuable as flowering advances. Historical grower observations describe limited stretch and a relatively favorable bud-to-leaf ratio, although individual phenotypes can differ. Moderate training early in vegetative growth can create additional productive tops, while aggressive late-flower manipulation offers little advantage with such a short maturation window.

BC Bud Depot repeatedly emphasizes heavy or maximum yields , although its current listing does not provide standardized grams-per-square-meter or grams-per-plant figures. For that reason, precise yield numbers often repeated by secondary databases should be viewed cautiously. Strong light, sufficient root space, balanced nutrition, stable temperatures, and humidity control will ultimately determine production more reliably than a strain-page estimate. Outdoors, the early September finish can be particularly useful in cooler northern climates where later cannabis varieties face increasing rain and falling temperatures.
FAQ
Is BC Sweet Tooth indica or sativa?

BC Bud Depot classifies it as 90% indica and 10% sativa, making it strongly indica dominant. Its effects can still begin with an uplifted or creative mental quality before becoming more physically relaxing.
What are the genetics of BC Sweet Tooth?

The breeder describes BC Sweet Tooth as an advancement of Sweet Tooth #3 (ST #3). Sweet Tooth #3 belongs to the Sweet Tooth genetic family associated with Sweet Pink Grapefruit and Blueberry-derived ancestry.
How strong is BC Sweet Tooth?

BC Bud Depot does not currently publish a standardized THC percentage. Secondary strain data commonly list flower around 24% THC, but actual potency should always be determined from laboratory testing of the specific batch.
What does BC Sweet Tooth taste like?
Candy sweetness forms the foundation, accompanied by flavors resembling honey, pear, berry, citrus, and mild earthy spice. The breeder specifically emphasizes dense buds with a sweet candy taste.
How long does BC Sweet Tooth take to flower?

Indoor flowering takes approximately six to seven weeks, and outdoor plants generally finish around early September according to BC Bud Depot. That unusually short cycle is one of the cultivar’s defining growing characteristics.
Final Thoughts on BC Sweet Tooth

BC Sweet Tooth belongs to an earlier generation of cannabis in which sweetness came from grapefruit, berries, honeyed fruit, and old-school resin rather than the pastry and candy-shop genetics that dominate much of today’s market. Its relationship to Sweet Tooth #3 gives it genuine breeding history, while BC Bud Depot’s further selection turned that heritage toward practical goals: fast flowering, dense buds, dependable production, and a strongly indica-dominant plant.

That combination remains useful decades after the Sweet Tooth family first gained attention. Growers receive a marijuana strain capable of completing bloom in only six to seven weeks, while consumers get an experience that can move from pleasant mental uplift into appetite, physical relaxation, and eventual sleepiness. Add its honeyed candy flavor and fruit-driven aroma, and BC Sweet Tooth earns its place not merely as another sweet weed strain, but as a surviving example of the British Columbia cannabis genetics that helped establish sweet, resinous indica hybrids long before today’s dessert-strain boom.
